long_biography.plain_text:
Intracom was conceived by Sokratis P. Kokkalis as a Greek centre for advanced technology, not merely an importer of communications equipment. Founded in 1977, the company reinvested heavily in proprietary research and manufacturing, then expanded through information technology, defence electronics, construction and energy infrastructure.

Kokkalis spent much of his youth as a political refugee in Romania and East Germany, where he studied physics and electronics before returning to Greece. He later established a Harvard programme focused on southeastern Europe and created the Kokkalis Foundation in memory of his father, surgeon and professor Petros Kokkalis. Its work concentrates on education and regional development.
